meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session November 24, 2025
meetings.presiding_chair: Chair Nida Allam (Note: Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee and Chair Nida Allam co-led/presided portions, with Nida Allam delivering the State of the County address)
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on November 24, 2025. The meeting featured the Annual State of the County Address presented collaboratively by the commissioners and Mayor Leonardo Williams, recognizing achievements across county departments and honoring County Manager Claudia Hager with the Order of the Long Leaf Pine. The board also conducted two public hearings, unanimously approving comprehensive Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) text amendments and a major general rezoning (Z250025) of the entire Research Triangle Park (RTP) to University and College-3 (UC-3) to facilitate a mixed-use, work-live-play vision. Additionally, the board approved a contract with Southern Wall Systems for exterior refurbishment and window replacement at the Durham County Justice Services Center.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgement, Pledge of Allegiance, and State of the County Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board convened for the regular session, reciting the public charge, land acknowledgement, and the Pledge of Allegiance. Chair Nida Alam delivered the State of the County Address, highlighting community resilience in response to recent ICE/CBP activity, recognizing new board members and County Manager Claudia Hager (who received the Order of the Long Leaf Pine), and reviewing county achievements and SNAP food drive successes.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Seth Kamansky as Durham County's Chief Paramedic
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized Seth Kamansky as Durham County's new Chief Paramedic in the Office of Emergency Services, highlighting his 16 years of experience in Wake County and emergency planning background. Commissioners welcomed him to the county.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Recognizing the 75th Anniversary of the Rougemont Ruritan Club
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented a commemorative resolution celebrating the 75th anniversary of the Rougemont Ruritan Club, recognizing its extensive community service, roadside cleanups, scholarships, and historic leadership including national presidents Millard Thacker and Lynward Hedgepath.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Private First Class Booker T. Spicely
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented a resolution honoring the life and legacy of Private First Class Booker T. Spicely, a Black World War II soldier killed in Durham in 1944 following a dispute over racial segregation on a bus, joined by civil rights attorney James Williams.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Adjusted)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved the adjusted consent agenda, with item 25-0595 pulled for separate public comment and deliberation regarding a contract for the Justice Services Center.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendments (Articles 4, 5, 6, 7) & Consistency Statement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a privately initiated Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) text amendment (TC25001 / RTP 3.0) to amend Articles 4, 5, 6, and 7 to create a new UC3 zoning district facilitating large scientific and technical research parks within the Research Triangle Park. The Board discussed data center definitions and standards before voting.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: RTP Rezoning (Z250025) & Consistency Statement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered a zoning map change request (Z250025) for the Research Triangle Park (RTP) rezoning, aligning with RTP existing covenants and establishing the UC3 zoning district. Following discussion and a consistency statement vote, the rezoning was unanimously approved.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Justice Services Center Exterior Refurbishment Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board discussed pulled consent item 25-0595, authorizing a contract with Southern Wall Systems LLC for $1,193,227 for exterior refurbishment and window replacement at the Durham County Justice Services Center. Public comments were heard before the Board unanimously approved the contract.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendments (Article 4, 5, 6, 7)
votes.mover: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.seconder: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.discussion_detail: The board considered an ordinance amendment incorporating revisions to the unified development ordinance across Article 4 (zoning districts), Article 5 (use regulations), Article 6 (district intensity standards), and Article 7 (design standards). Discussion touched upon limited use standards for new data centers, including distance from residential areas and noise studies, while grandfathering existing facilities. Following discussion, a motion was made and properly seconded to adopt the ordinance amendment. The motion passed unanimously with no recorded nays.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendments Consistency Statement
votes.mover: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.seconder: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.discussion_detail: Following the adoption of the UDO text amendments, the board took up the required consistency statement under North Carolina General Statute section 160D-605. A motion was made and properly seconded to adopt the consistency statement. The motion passed unanimously with no recorded nays.

votes.item_title: RTP Rezoning (Z250025)
votes.mover: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.seconder: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.discussion_detail: The board addressed the rezoning request (Case Z250025) for the entirety of Research Triangle Park (RTP) except for the Durham County Wildlife Club parcel, covering just over 5,000 acres including rights-of-way. The proposal rezoned the area from various classifications—including science and research park, industrial light, and residential districts—to the newly adopted University and College-3 district. Following staff presentation and discussion regarding comprehensive land use plan alignment and future visioning, a motion to adopt the ordinance amendment was made, seconded, and passed unanimously.

votes.mover: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.seconder: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.discussion_detail: In connection with the RTP rezoning request (Z250025), the board considered the adoption of the consistency statement required by North Carolina General Statute section 160D-605. A motion was made and properly seconded to adopt the consistency statement. The motion passed unanimously in a voice vote with no recorded nays.

votes.item_title: Justice Services Center Exterior Refurbishment Contract
votes.mover: Not specified by name in voice vote
votes.seconder: Not specified by name in voice vote

Prior to the vote, public comments were received regarding community concerns. Following discussion, a motion was made and properly seconded to approve the item, which passed unanimously with no recorded nays.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session November 3, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham County Board of Commissioners held a work session on November 3, 2025, hearing extensive public comment from northern Durham residents regarding concerns over the Durham-to-Roxboro rail-to-trail project. The board suspended rules and unanimously approved grant agreements, budget ordinance amendments, capital project amendments, and a TIP agreement with NC DOT to acquire the 26-mile Durham-to-Roxboro rail corridor. Additionally, the board discussed capital improvement plans, debt management, bond ratings, and received presentations on the county's financial outlook and the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) vision plan.

agenda_items.title: Durham-to-Roxboro Rail-to-Trail Acquisition & State Grant Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board discussed public comments opposing the Durham-to-Roxboro rail-to-trail project, followed by a staff presentation and board deliberation on authorizing the chair's signature on the Great Trails State Grant Program agreement ($500,000) and approving capital/budget amendments and TIP agreement with NCDOT for rail corridor acquisition. Commissioners emphasized the long-standing vision, massive outside grant leverage (net local cost of $223,000 or 1.7%), and future transportation preservation.

agenda_items.title: Financial Management & Bond Rating Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board received a presentation and discussed county financial management, debt policies, credit ratings (AAA market access), and investment statutory frameworks with financial consultants and staff.

agenda_items.title: Durham Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Vision Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board received an overview and update on the Durham Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Vision Plan from transportation staff and consultants, discussing corridor prioritization and enhanced transit service.

votes.item_title: Suspend rules for consideration of grant and corridor acquisition items
votes.discussion_detail: The Board considered a procedural motion to suspend the rules to allow for immediate consideration of grant and corridor acquisition items, moving swiftly to advance time-sensitive matters. The motion was moved by Commissioner Burton and seconded by Commissioner Valentine, passing unanimously with no opposing votes. This procedural step preceded discussions and approvals regarding the Great Trails State Grant Program and the Durham-to-Roxboro rail corridor acquisition.

votes.item_title: Authorize chair signature on Great Trails State Grant Program agreement ($500,000)
votes.discussion_detail: The Board voted to authorize the chair's signature on the Great Trails State Grant Program agreement with the North Carolina Department of Natural and Cultural Resources to accept $500,000 in grant funding. The motion was moved by Commissioner Valentine and seconded by Vice Chair Dr. Lee, passing unanimously. Staff subsequently explained that the funding relates to trail planning and development efforts overseen by the transportation department.

votes.item_title: Approve budget ordinance amendment 26BCC029, capital project amendment 26CPA009, and TIP agreement with NC DOT for Durham-to-Roxboro rail corridor acquisition
votes.discussion_detail: The Board approved budget ordinance amendment number 26BCC029, capital project amendment number 26CPA009, and the TIP agreement with the North Carolina Department of Transportation (NC DOT) for the acquisition of the Durham-to-Roxboro rail corridor. Transportation Director Ellen Beckman, planner Brooke Roer, and NC DOT manager Hart Evans outlined the project details, noting a total TIP agreement amount of $1,151,445 with a net county expenditure of $223,000 and recognized state grants of $928,445. Staff explained that due to NC DOT's scheduled closing on November 19th, the county was asked to pay the TIP agreement about a week ahead of schedule. The motion was moved by Commissioner Burns and seconded by Commissioner Valentine, and passed unanimously.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Budget Work Session May 22th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: On day two of its FY26 budget work session, the Board of County Commissioners heard budget presentations and operational updates from the Office of the Sheriff, the Office of Emergency Services (OES), and the Durham County Youth Home. Commissioners questioned department leaders extensively on fleet replacement costs and tariff impacts, 89 detention officer vacancies and mandatory overtime, rising EMS call volumes and response times, Medicaid Tailored Plan billing delays, and aligning growth planning with emergency service capacity. No formal motions or votes were taken during this work session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Office of the Sheriff Law Enforcement Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam opened day two of the budget work session and invited Sheriff Clarence Birkhead to present. Before beginning the budget overview, Captain Carpenter updated the board on the apprehension of a suspect in a recent Red Mill Road homicide, and Captain Webster described Durham deputies assisting Chatham County during a nine-hour standoff on an involuntary commitment call. Commissioners Wendy Jacobs, Michelle Burton, and Stephen Valentine asked about response protocols for mental health histories, prior calls at the residence, and community intelligence used in the arrest.

agenda_items.title: Office of the Sheriff FY26 Budget Presentation and Detention Center Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sheriff Birkhead presented FY26 budget priorities, highlighting recommended funding for 34 EcoBoost SUVs and fleet replacements, a $343,200 vehicle maintenance increase, and five new deputy positions for an RTP zone funded via position realignment, alongside unfunded requests including detention center kitchen repairs, stab-resistant vests, Cellbrite, uniforms, BeyondTrust IT software, and additional training. Commissioners pressed staff on vehicle replacement lifecycles, factory recalls, tariff price projections, the estimated $500,000 RTP tax district contribution, HEART co-response expansion resourcing, and jail food service contracting. Significant discussion also focused on the detention center's 89 vacancies out of 224 FTEs, mandatory overtime, single-officer pod staffing, mental health screening rates near 70%, officer wellness, and commissioner visits to the jail.

agenda_items.title: Office of Emergency Services (OES) FY26 Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Manager Dwayne Brenson and OES Director Mark Lockhart presented OES highlights and FY26 budget requests, covering ambulance deliveries with 30-to-36-month lead times, relocating the Stone Park Court fleet facility by December 1 due to railroad relocation, TDMA portable radio upgrades ahead of the July 1 deadline, and an estimated $2.3 million revenue pipeline backlog caused by North Carolina's Medicaid Tailored Plan billing transition. Recommended budget items included a senior auto mechanic via relief position realignment, an emergency management deputy chief, 12 FTEs (6 EMTs and 6 paramedics) to staff one new 24-hour transport unit, five replacement ambulances, and four replacement SUVs, alongside data showing a 24.7% call volume increase since FY18 and average emergent response times hovering near 8 minutes (90th percentile around 13 minutes). Commissioners questioned staff on public safety recruitment and pay competitiveness against Wake County, community paramedicine, and integrating EMS and first responder infrastructure impacts into Planning Department development reviews.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Youth Home FY26 Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Director Angela Nunn began the Durham County Youth Home presentation, reporting that the facility successfully opened two pods totaling 24 beds after transitioning 14 residents in 2024 and plans to open two additional pods later as staffing expands. She also highlighted that the new Youth Home achieved LEED Platinum certification in April 2025 for its energy, water, and indoor environmental performance before the video recording concluded.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham BOCC Budget Work Session May 22th, 2025
disagreements.issue: Budgeting and Capacity Expansion for HEART Co-Response Pilot
disagreements.summary: Commissioners expressed differing emphases on whether to include resource allocations for a Sheriff's Office HEART co-response expansion pilot in the current budget cycle versus waiting for data analysis and context from the City of Durham's pilot.
disagreements.side_a_position: Include resourcing requirements in the budget if a HEART expansion pilot is a department priority
side_a_arguments: Running any pilot or trial of HEART expansion in the county will require identifiable resourcing.
Waiting through repeated planning meetings without seeing resource needs reflected in the budget delays action and makes outcome evaluation harder next year.
disagreements.side_b_position: Exercise caution on expanding capacity until data analysis, RFP findings, and City pilot context are reviewed
side_b_arguments: When the City of Durham conducted its HEART pilot, it did not expand capacity.
Understanding what the City's pilot actually required in resourcing should inform what Durham County commits to once the data analysis and RFP work are completed.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken during the work session; county staff indicated they would return to the board with HEART evaluation analytics and either realign existing positions or request a mid-year adjustment if needed.

The application requested a county rezoning of 13.96 acres from residential, rural, and commercial neighborhood to commercial general with a textual development plan, receiving a unanimous recommendation of approval from the planning commission. Commissioners acknowledged planning staff's adaptation to recent state legislation and landowner outreach for this transit-oriented area site. Following discussion regarding access points, utilities, and first responder fiscal impacts, the ordinance passed unanimously (5-0).

votes.item_title: East Club at I-85 Rezoning (Consistency Statement)
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Burton moved to adopt the required consistency statement under North Carolina General Statute Section 160D-605 for the East Club at I-85 rezoning request, seconded by Commissioner Jacobs. The 13.96-acre rezoning from residential, rural, and commercial neighborhood to commercial general with a textual development plan was previously reviewed as a transit-oriented area project. Commissioners discussed the planning staff's work amidst changing state legislation and raised administrative questions regarding how future rezonings assess fiscal impacts on first responders like EMS, fire, and sheriff's deputies. votes.item_title: Page Miami Design District Text Amendment (Ordinance)
votes.discussion_detail: The Board considered a motion to adopt an ordinance amending the Unified Development Ordinance incorporating revisions to Article 11 science standards and Article 16 design districts. The applicant agreed to prohibit drive-thru facilities and gas sales as an oversight correction to ensure low-intensity uses. Following the vote, commissioners raised questions regarding the lack of fiscal impact analyses for first responders (EMS, fire, and sheriff's deputies) during rezonings, to which planning staff member Sarah Young explained that developing a rezoning fiscal impact process is an ongoing implementation action from the comprehensive plan. The motion passed unanimously (5-0).

votes.item_title: Page Miami Design District Text Amendment (Consistency Statement)
votes.discussion_detail: The Board considered a motion to adopt the required statutory consistency statement under North Carolina General Statute section 160D-605 for the Page Miami Design District Text Amendment. disagreements.issue: Text amendment to allow adjustments to tree protection and tree coverage standards via development agreements.
disagreements.summary: Commissioners debated whether allowing tree coverage adjustments in development agreements provides vital flexibility for affordable housing or undermines environmental protections and tree canopy retention.
side_a_arguments: Necessary flexibility to support affordable housing (specifically Low-Income Housing Tax Credit projects on tight sites where parking and tree save requirements conflict) and maintain consistency with city approvals and joint planning policies.
side_b_arguments: Concerns over loss of tree canopy, exacerbating the construction sediment crisis in Southeast Durham, stormwater runoff, setting a poor precedent, and bypassing UDO tree protection standards.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Transit Plan FY 2026 Work Program Update

votes.item_title: Move into Closed Session
votes.mover: Not explicitly named in transcript text

disagreements.issue: Proposal to name a building or facility after former Mayor and Commissioner William V. 'Bill' Bell
disagreements.summary: Discussion regarding whether to name a county building or lobby in honor of Bill Bell, balancing his historic contributions against existing county naming policies and coordination across local government bodies.
disagreements.side_a_position: Strong support for naming a county building or prominent space in honor of Bill Bell to recognize his extraordinary lifetime of service.
side_a_arguments: Bill Bell was a transformational leader who shaped modern Durham through the city-county school merger and decades of public service.
As Durham evolves and new residents arrive, collective memory fades without prominent physical landmarks.
disagreements.side_b_position: Cautious stance supporting recognition via a lobby plaque/portrait while expressing hesitation toward naming entire buildings amidst multiple multi-agency campaigns and policy exceptions.
side_b_arguments: Concerns over multiple concurrent naming efforts and campaigns across different local governing bodies (city, county, and school board).
Importance of adhering to established county naming policies and ensuring equitable recognition of other long-serving commissioners.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken during this work session; discussion deferred for further coordination and scheduling at an upcoming meeting.

Project Manager Joel Jones discussed the project timeline, noting that construction was expected to span approximately 24 months following kickoff. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs questioned aspects of the training facility project, leading to a contested debate regarding expenditures and facility planning. Dissenting members Wendy Jacobs and Michelle Burton voted NAY on the contract, expressing concerns over project scope and costs. meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on March 10, 2025, discussing federal funding and policy impacts, hearing public comments on property tax revaluations, adopting several monthly proclamations (Ramadan, National Social Work Month, and Women's History Month), approving the consent agenda including capital project amendments for school general obligation bonds, and receiving a presentation on the 2024 City-County Resident Survey results.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Land Acknowledgement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Alam called the regular session to order, read the public charge regarding respectful behavior, and Commissioner Burton delivered the land acknowledgement recognizing indigenous peoples.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Alam introduced an agenda adjustment to add a Ramadan proclamation. Clerk Wallace read county announcements regarding property reappraisal notices, upcoming community events, library programs, and youth budget art contests. Commissioners Jacobs and Burton also shared updates from the National Association of Counties (NACo) legislative conference.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Motion to approve agenda adjustment with Ramadan Proclamation added)

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Residents signed up to speak addressed the board. Victoria Peterson raised concerns regarding the distribution and transparency of federal funding (ARPA/COVID relief funds) and support for local organizations and seniors.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed and considered the approval of the meeting minutes from the February 24, 2025 Regular Session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Moved by Commissioner Valentine, seconded by Vice Chair Dr. Lee)

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items & Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board presented several ceremonial proclamations, including a Ramadan Proclamation, a proclamation recognizing Social Work Month (featuring DSS Director Maggie Clapp), and a proclamation recognizing Women's History Month.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (ceremonial presentations and proclamations)

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the consent agenda, which included capital project amendments for school obligation bonds (DSA). Commissioner Jacobs pulled items 25-01 through 25-03 for discussion regarding school capital project funding and updates.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Moved by Commissioner Burton, seconded by Vice Chair Lee)

agenda_items.title: Presentation: 2024 City-County Resident Satisfaction Survey
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and representatives presented the results of the 10th consecutive City-County Resident Satisfaction Survey, detailing community feedback on county services, safety, schools, and quality of life. Commissioners discussed survey findings and community engagement.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (presentation and discussion only)

agenda_items.title: Board Closing Comments and Excused Absences
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners made closing remarks regarding the upcoming budget cycle. Commissioner Jacobs and Chair Alam requested excused absences for upcoming meetings (March 24 regular session and April 7 work session), which were approved by the board.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Excused absences approved for Commissioner Jacobs and Chair Alam)

votes.item_title: Agenda Adjustment (Add Ramadan Proclamation)
votes.discussion_detail: During the opening of the regular session, the chair requested an agenda adjustment to add a proclamation recognizing Ramadan 2025, which had been emailed to the clerk prior to the meeting. The board members indicated their approval without opposition, and the motion to approve the agenda as amended passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Approval of February 24, 2025 Meeting Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: The board considered the approval of the meeting minutes from the February 24, 2025 regular session. Commissioner Valentine moved to approve the minutes, with a second provided by Vice Chair Dr. Lee. The minutes were approved unanimously by the board without any opposition.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence Request for Commissioner Jacobs
votes.discussion_detail: Toward the end of the meeting, Commissioner Jacobs requested an excused absence for the upcoming March 24th regular session and April 7th work session. The motion for approval was moved and seconded, and all members present voted in favor. The motion passed unanimously without opposition.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence Request for Chair Nida Alam
votes.discussion_detail: During the discussion on meeting absences, Chair Nida Alam noted that she would also need to request an excused absence for the April 7th session. A motion to approve her absence was seconded by Commissioner Valentine and passed unanimously. Vice Chair Lee confirmed she would lead the meeting on that date.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (Feb 3 Work Session and Feb 10 Regular Session)

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session Feb 10th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held their regular session on February 10, 2025, presided over by Chair Nida Allam. The board adopted the meeting agenda, received extensive community and county service announcements, introduced Evan Kramer as the new Durham Memorial Stadium manager, issued a proclamation designating February 2025 as Black History Month, and unanimously adopted a solemn resolution honoring the lives and legacy of Shadi Barakat, Yusor Muhammad Abu-Salha, and Razan Muhammad Abu-Salha on the 10th anniversary of their passing.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Land Acknowledgement, Pledge of Allegiance, and Announcements

Clerk Pastor Cler Wallace presented the weekly announcements including Deco Cares applications, transit work plan public input, Black History Month events, farmland protection plan public engagement, and tax administration deadlines.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Motion to approve the agenda moved by Commissioner Burton, seconded by Commissioner Valentine, approved unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of Durham County Memorial Stadium Manager Evan Kramer
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services Deputy Director Crystal Thomas introduced Evan Kramer as the new Stadium Manager for Durham County Memorial Stadium. agenda_items.title: Black History Month Proclamation (February 2025)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Burton read a proclamation designating February 2025 as Black History Month in Durham County. agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Deah Barakat, Yusor Muhammad Abu-Salha, and Razan Muhammad Abu-Salha (10th Anniversary)

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session Feb 3rd, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its Work Session on February 3, 2025. The board heard public comments regarding Black History Month, public records, and the foster care/family policing system. During the consent agenda review, commissioners discussed details regarding the youth home subsidy rates, open space matching grants, and property management agreements. The board voted to suspend the rules and delegate authority to the county attorney to execute a contract amendment with Arthur J. Gallagher risk management company. Finally, the board received major presentations on the Durham Convention Center and headquarter hotel market and financial feasibility study, the FY 2026 Transit Work Program, and the County food security initiatives implementation update.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Land Acknowledgment, and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Lee called the meeting to order, read the public charge, and Commissioner Burton read the land acknowledgement. The board held a moment of silence in honor of Captain Rebecca Lobach and other victims of a tragic helicopter collision.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Three public speakers addressed the board: James Chavis invited the county manager to a townhouse meeting on Black History Month and county budget; Rafi Zadi requested public records regarding carbon monoxide investigations at the DSS facility; and Amanda Wallace raised concerns regarding children in the family policing system and Durham DSS.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy manager Maurice Gough presented consent agenda items, including battery purchase contracts, health budget amendments for the 2026 community health assessment, youth home MOAs, IT disaster recovery contracts, utility agreements, lease amendments for China Walk, open space matching grants, and property management agreements. Commissioners asked questions regarding youth home per diem costs, open space grants, and retail property leasing.

agenda_items.title: County Food Security Initiatives Implementation Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County food security coordinator Reena Goldstein-Bug and Donna Rewalt presented an implementation update on county food security initiatives, reviewing food security definitions, rates, arpa-related food security projects, and future plans.

agenda_items.title: Gallagher Risk Management Contract Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a request to renew the annual insurance brokerage and risk management consulting contract with Arthur J. Gallagher Risk Management Services. The board discussed the importance of protecting immunities while maintaining proper insurance coverage.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Suspension of rules passed unanimously; delegation of authority passed unanimously)

agenda_items.title: Durham County Convention Center and Headquarter Hotel Feasibility Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Gina propes (City of Durham) and Sean Gerson (Hunden Partners) presented the findings of the Durham Convention Center and Headquarter Hotel market and financial feasibility study. The study highlighted economic impacts of over $5 billion in net new spending over 30 years and 1,100 jobs per year. Commissioners discussed hotel capacity, walkability, community inclusion, and funding strategies.

agenda_items.title: Review of County Commissioner Directives & Meeting Wrap-up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of staff Trap reviewed board directives and received new suggestions from commissioners regarding mapping housing growth alongside service capacity (EMS, fire, sheriff, schools) and updating the agenda format to include commissioner comments.

agenda_items.title: FY 2026 Transit Work Program Presentation & Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and city transportation representatives presented the FY 2026 Transit Work Program draft, covering goDurham and goTriangle updates, brt plans, bus stop improvements, and budget allocations. Commissioners raised significant concerns regarding cost increases, increased allocation to operations & maintenance vs going more places, project delivery transparency, and accountability metrics.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Draft work program release previously approved 3-1 with Durham County voting against

agenda_items.title: RISE Assessment Center at the Youth Home Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Angela Mckinney and Jennifer McCant presented an update on the Resources for Youth Success and Empowerment (RISE) Assessment Center at the youth home, detailing walk-in/appointment services, diversion programs, upcoming summer 2025 comprehensive rollout using the CANS assessment tool, and extended operational hours.

votes.item_title: Suspend rules for Gallagher risk management contract amendment
votes.mover: Vice Chair Dr. Nida Allam (or Dr. Lee)
votes.discussion_detail: The Board considered a procedural motion to suspend the rules regarding a contract amendment with Arthur J. Gallagher Risk Management Services, LLC through January 9, 2026, in the amount of $42,000 for insurance brokerage and risk management services. Staff noted that the renewal rate and proposal remained the same as the previous year, maintaining proper immunities and insurance coverage. The motion to suspend the rules was moved by Vice Chair Dr. Lee, seconded by Commissioner Valentine, and passed unanimously with no opposition.

votes.item_title: Delegate authority to county attorney to execute contract amendment with Arthur J. Gallagher risk management company
votes.seconder: Vice Chair Dr. Nida Allam (Dr. Lee)
votes.discussion_detail: Following the suspension of rules, the Board considered delegating authority to the county attorney to execute the contract amendment with Arthur J. Gallagher Risk Management Services, LLC through January 9, 2026, in the amount of $42,000. Staff explained that the agreement continues the previous year's terms and rates to properly navigate immunities and ensure adequate coverage. The motion was moved by Commissioner Jacobs, seconded by Vice Chair Dr. Lee, and approved unanimously by the Board.

disagreements.issue: Concerns over the FY 2026 Transit Work Program allocations, increasing operations & maintenance share vs going more places, and reporting/accountability metrics.
disagreements.summary: Debate over transit plan priorities, funding transparency, and accountability between commissioners and transit staff.
disagreements.side_a_position: Opposed to draft transit allocations and lack of delivery metrics without accountability
side_a_arguments: Commissioners expressed strong concerns that the draft FY 2026 transit work plan shifts 50% away from expanding service ("going more places") toward operations and maintenance, lacks clear project delivery metrics and accountability, and relies heavily on county funds/transit tax without adequate city skin in the game.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defending the draft plan structure while acknowledging need for refined schedules and reporting tools
side_b_arguments: Staff explained that the schedule reflects ongoing commitments, interlocal agreements involve a complex multi-agency process, and a Transit Tracker website is in development to improve reporting.
disagreements.resolution: Discussion only; items presented for information/review ahead of April decisions.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session Jan 13th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its regular session on January 13, 2025, adopting the agenda, minutes, and a resolution honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. The board debated and approved two pulled consent items: $16.5 million in limited obligation bond funding for the Sheriff's training facility (Item 24-0645, passed 3-2 after extensive debate on accountability and 911 dispatch duplication) and a preconstruction services contract for the new Durham County Emergency Operations Center (Item 24-0789, passed unanimously).

agenda_items.title: Opening, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgement, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The meeting was called to order with the reading of the public charge and indigenous land acknowledgement, followed by the Pledge of Allegiance and approval of the agenda. Clerk Wallace then presented extensive community announcements including the upcoming DC Thrive guaranteed income launch, MLK Day celebrations, food security grants, and planning department office hours.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (approval of agenda passed unanimously)

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board read and formally adopted a resolution honoring the life, legacy, and impact of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., highlighting his civil rights advocacy in Durham and recommitting the county to racial equity, affordable housing, living wages, and humane labor conditions.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the consent agenda excluding items pulled for separate discussion: Capital Project Amendment No. 25 for the Sheriff's Training Facility and the contract for preconstruction services for the new Emergency Operations Center / backup 911 call center.

agenda_items.title: Contract for Preconstruction Services for New Durham County EOC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board discussed Item 24-0789 regarding preconstruction services for the new Durham County Emergency Operations Center (EOC) and backup 911 call center. Commissioners raised questions about potential service duplication with the existing Joint City-County Durham Emergency Communications Center (DECC) and the additional $4.5 million cost for a separate sheriff's backup call center, while staff noted design flexibility moving forward.

agenda_items.title: Capital Project Amendment No. 25 - Sheriff's Training Facility \$16.5M LOB Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board engaged in extensive deliberation on Capital Project Amendment No. 25 (CPA 2022) allocating $16.5 million in Limited Obligation Bonds (LOBs) for the Durham County Sheriff's Training Facility (Item 24-0645). Public commenters and Commissioner Jacobs raised concerns regarding accountability, transparency, jail conditions, and demands for expanding the HEART mental health crisis response program into the county rather than funding separate facilities. Proponents emphasized staff mandates, deputy training needs, and public safety across all neighborhoods.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 3-2 (Commissioners Alam, Valentine, and Burton voting Aye; Commissioners Jacobs and Lee voting No)

agenda_items.title: Meeting Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the conclusion of agenda business and votes, the board entertained a motion for adjournment.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (motion to adjourn passed unanimously)

votes.item_title: Capital Project Amendment No. 25 (CPA 2022) - $16.5M LOB funding for Durham County Sheriff's Training Facility (Item 24-0645)
votes.notes: Approved after extensive public comment and board debate regarding accountability, 911 dispatch duplication, and HEART expansion.
votes.discussion_detail: Capital Project Amendment No. 25 (CPA 2022) proposed appropriating $16.5 million in LOB funding for the Durham County Sheriff's Training Facility (Item 24-0645). Commissioners discussed accountability and transparency expectations surrounding the Sheriff's Office, referencing prior recommendations from the community safety and wellness task force. Commissioner Valentine emphasized treating the constitutional sheriff as a professional partner in governance while focusing strictly on role and function. Commissioners Nida Allam and Wendy Jacobs voted in opposition due to community concerns regarding accountability and transparency, whereas Dr. Lee moved approval and Nzinga A. Valentine seconded. The motion ultimately passed by a 3-2 vote.

votes.item_title: Contract for Preconstruction Services for New Durham County EOC (Item 24-0789)
votes.notes: Authorized county manager to execute contract for preconstruction services for the new Durham County Emergency Operations Center.
votes.discussion_detail: Item 24-0789 authorized the county manager to execute a contract with the team for preconstruction services for the new Durham County Emergency Operations Center (EOC). Vice chair Dr. Lee moved approval of the item, which was seconded by commissioner Valentine. Following discussion on previous matters, the board called for a vote with all members in favor and none opposed. The contract authorization passed unanimously.

disagreements.issue: Funding for Durham County Sheriff's training facility ($16.5M Limited Obligation Bonds) versus demands for accountability, transparency, 911 call center consolidation, and HEART mental health crisis response expansion.
disagreements.summary: Debate over $16.5M LOB funding for the Sheriff's training facility, balancing law enforcement training needs and statutory funding against community demands for accountability, 911 consolidation, and HEART expansion.
disagreements.side_a_position: Opposed funding the Sheriff's training facility until accountability and service integration issues are addressed.
side_a_arguments: Concerns over lack of accountability and responsiveness from the Sheriff's office, duplicative 911/backup center costs ($4.5M for separate sheriff backup vs consolidated DECC), and need for full countywide expansion of the HEART program.
disagreements.side_b_position: Supported funding the Sheriff's training facility as a vital capital improvement project.
side_b_arguments: Training facility is a necessary state-mandated capital improvement for law enforcement, provides safe and proper training, addresses community safety concerns regarding gun violence, and respects the Sheriff as an elected constitutional officer.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 3-2 with Commissioners Lee, Valentine, and Burton voting aye, and Chair Allam and Commissioner Jacobs voting nay.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Work Session Jan 6th, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held its Work Session on January 6, 2025, presided over by Chair Nida Allam. The board heard extensive public comments concerning public safety, funding for the Sheriff's Office training facility, and the HEART unarmed crisis response program. Staff presented updates on the upcoming property tax revaluation (schedule of values, tax relief programs, and commercial/residential property trends) and a review of the Sheriff's Office training facility project and budget. No formal roll call votes or motions were recorded during this work session, as business items were previewed for upcoming regular meetings.

agenda_items.title: Meeting Opening, Public Charge, and Land Acknowledgement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Alam called the Durham County Board of Commissioners work session to order for January 6, 2025. Commissioner Burton read the public charge regarding respectful conduct, followed by a land acknowledgement recognizing indigenous peoples.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Numerous residents and community advocates spoke during citizen comments. Major topics included urging the board not to fund the $16 million Sheriff's training facility expansion, advocating for the expansion of the HEART program countywide, expressing concerns over detention center conditions and medical costs, and discussing community engagement surrounding the firing range.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review and Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed and discussed various consent agenda items, including detention center healthcare overages, interlocal agreements, library grants, the Alliance Health contract for mental health and substance use services, and the capital project amendment for the Sheriff's training facility. Commissioners asked clarifying questions regarding medical cost drivers and consent agenda procedures.

agenda_items.title: Updated Presentation on the Sheriff's Training Facility Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County engineering staff, the Sheriff's Office planning director, and architects presented an updated overview of the Durham County Sheriff's training facility project and guaranteed maximum price contract. Staff reviewed site history on a former landfill, environmental assessments, lead capture systems, firing range modernization, secure impound storage, and classroom spaces for recruit and inservice training.

agenda_items.title: Presentation on 2025 Property Revaluation and Tax Relief Programs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tax Administration staff presented an update on the 2025 property revaluation process, commercial and residential market trends, upcoming public informational meeting dates, and state property tax relief programs along with Durham's low-income homeowner relief program. Commissioners discussed homeowner tax burden, statutory income limits for elderly/disabled exemptions, and revenue-neutral tax rate mechanics.
